task: Plan 13.1 increment (researcher-evidenced with 4 runtime receipts): numbered size refusals and a bounded fallback reply in the shared human/AI transport, so an AI operator can tell how much to trim and a transport overflow can never stop the session or hide that an operation may have executed
purpose: Live refusals read {"ok":false,"error":"ValueError: JSON exceeds the protocol size limit","request_sha256":null}, naming neither the 131072-byte request limit (client_protocol.py:15) nor the actual byte count, so an operator cannot tell how much to trim. Second, same family: client_bridge._one() wrote the reply via wire.atomic() OUTSIDE the try/except, so an oversize reply (>1 MiB) escaped to poll() which called stop(): session died, no response file, and for an apply whose operator already ran (record embeds full inspect(), operations.py ~780) the caller could not tell whether the edit executed. Player benefit: actionable numbers on refusals; the recovery contract (OPERATIONS.md: a missing reply is an unknown outcome, never an automatic repeat) stays enforceable.
